headline: Zero percent of Ward 45's menu money went to sidewalks, even with strong safety numbers.
summary:
Jefferson Park, Forest Glen, Portage Park and Norwood Park make up Ward 45, on the Northwest Side, landing ninth in the citywide count of fifty. Residents here report some of the lowest loneliness rates anywhere in Chicago. The ward also comes in second-lowest on violent crime and third-best on feeling safe walking alone at night. It put nearly all of its menu money into street resurfacing last year, behind only one other ward.

Everything else in Ward 45 runs thinner. The ward spent none of its menu money on sidewalks or on bike and pedestrian projects, and it runs no participatory budgeting process for residents to vote on how that money gets spent, though most Chicago wards skip that too. Response time on rodent baiting requests and the property tax dollars captured by TIF districts also sit close to the bottom of the list.
reading_the_rankings: Take the loneliness figure first, where Ward 45 posts the lowest rate in the city. It comes from spreading a census survey across each tract by land area rather than by actual population, so a slice of the number may really belong to a neighboring ward, and its own confidence grade comes in low. The violent crime rank, second-best citywide, rests on that same tract-by-area method, and here the source marks it only medium confidence. The ward's 49th of 50 finish on participatory budgeting looks worse on paper than it plays out in practice. Walk down the list from Ward 45's spot at 49th and you can cross off thirty-seven wards before the score moves two points, because most of Chicago never set up a participatory budgeting vote to begin with.

news.headline: Boy, 13, Wounded In Portage Park Drive-By Shooting
news.note: A 13-year-old was shot in the leg on Montrose Avenue in Portage Park, with no arrests reported at the time of the story.

news.headline: Historic Jefferson Park Firehouse Could Be Turned Into Salon Suite For Local Businesses
news.note: A developer proposed converting the ground floor of a 120-year-old firehouse into a shared beauty and wellness space for about 15 local businesses.

news.headline: Jeff Fest Is No More. It's The Chicago Italian Beef Fest Now
news.note: Jefferson Park's 25-year-old music and arts festival was rebranded around Italian beef, with eight vendors set for the late-July event.
